newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - T-bonds' near-term momentum faltering.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bonds' near-term momentum faltering.

text.p: Shorter-term momentum indicators for U.S. Treasury bond futures are starting to falter, signaling that the market may finally correct its overbought condition, technical analysts said.

Various oscillators had been flashing overbought signals since early June, they said, but the market's strong upward trend momentum had overrun those indications so far, as typically happens in a bull market.
"Now because the directional momentum is waning, the overbought condition is moving to the forefront," said Terence Gabriel, a technical analyst at I.D.E.A.
He said the daily Bollinger band width was shrinking to critical levels and the ADX trend-strength indicator had stopped expanding.

"It looks like we've had a near-term reversal in the last couple of days," said Jim Bohan, senior financial futures strategist at Merrill Lynch Capital Markets, agreeing that the market's momentum appeared to be stalling.

"This is probably the start of a consolidation phase," he added. "We could spend the next two to three weeks in some sort of a trading range-type pattern in order to consolidate the move up from early June and the move up from April."
Bohan saw 110 to 110-1/2, the base of the early-June breakout, as a likely near-term support for September T-bonds.
Gabriel expected 111-15/32, the lower end of a steep upward channel from the late-May bottom, to be good support.

He added that the contract was unlikely to pull back so deep as to test the lower boundaries of less steep channels formed in the earlier stages of the market's rally from April lows. That support would come in at the 109-110 area.
The September contract was off 1/32 at 112-4/32 in mid-morning trade, after dipping as low as 111-29/32.
Gabriel predicted that within a few weeks the market would test the February 18 high of 113-9/32 and the trendline drawn from January 1996, currently coming in in the mid-113s.

The outlook was similar for the shorter end of the yield curve, with December Eurodollar futures grinding to a halt after the sharp June 12-13 rally. The contract stood at 93.945, up 0.005 point, in late morning business.

Gabriel said a retreat toward 93.90 or 93.85 would probably be a good buying opportunity, given the likelihood of an eventual retest of the trendline from December 1996 highs, currently coming in at 93.99.
